title: Yachid, Echad, Kadmon: the sefiros that are not in the Essence and cannot be taken out of it
overview:
The series begins here. Its introduction calls *Shaar HaYichud* a book in two parts: what *hisbonenus* is (not meditation but *iyun*, detailed analytical study, as a doctor must know every particular), and, from chapter 10, what to contemplate: every world and every *sefira* in particulars.

The chapter starts at the top, with the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, in three levels, *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*. The texts say there are no ten *sefiros* there, and they say He engraved letters there, a *Keser* and a *Malchus*. The answer is the kind man. His kindness is not made of kindnesses for shoes and sandwiches; yet a kindness that will not do shoes is no kindness at all, "just a bureaucracy", and the pants he never gave are in it too. So with the *Aibershter*: take out one *sefira* and you are a *kofer*; and in the *nimshal* the actual sandwich, the actual car, comes from there. In the soul the same three levels run from powers that *mamash* do not exist, through powers ready to come out, to the estimate of one grab for the vodka bottle; and to reach the physical it takes a *tzimtzum*.

sections.title: From here on: every world, every sefira, in particulars
sections.summary: The first part of the book taught that *hisbonenus* is detailed study; from chapter 10 the book begins the subject itself, the four worlds and their *sefiros* down to particulars of particulars, and how each world's *Keser* joins it to the one above.

phrases.he: (י) ומעתה הנה יש להבין דרך פרט
phrases.en: So now he's going to explain in the *derech prat*.

phrases.he: בכל ד' עולמות דאבי''ע,
דהיינו בכל פרטי ענין עשר ספירות דאבי''ע
אורות וכלים והתלבשותן זה בזה
בכל פרטיהן,
phrases.en: He's going to explain all the particulars.

כמו גם בבחינת חסד דמלכות שבחכמה שבמלכות דחסד וכהאי גוונא

blocks.text: *Shaar HaYichud*, the Gate of Unification, by the *Mitteler Rebbe*, Rabbi DovBer, the second Lubavitcher Rebbe, is called the Key to Kabbala and *Chassidus*, and *Kuntres HaHisbonenus*, the book of contemplation. Part one, what *hisbonenus* (contemplation) is, continues his *Kuntres HaHispaalus*: there is no real *hispaalus* (awakening of the G-dly emotions, love and fear) without proper *hisbonenus* first. Part two, from chapter 10, is what to contemplate.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the introduction to the series (tape 001), which reads no line: it presents the book and says why the classes begin at chapter 10, so it is placed under the chapter's opening.

blocks.text: *Hisbonenus* is not, as most people think, meditation, which is concentration, but what the Talmud calls *iyun*: deep, repetitive, analytical study, going over a subject again and again in slightly new ways, finding new angles.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the introduction to the series (tape 001), which reads no line: it presents the book and says why the classes begin at chapter 10, so it is placed under the chapter's opening.

blocks.title: The doctor and the engineer
blocks.text: Knowing in general what medicine or engineering is does not make you a doctor or an engineer. A doctor must know every part of the body, every medicine and malady, and which medicine works for which. So with any subject: the deeper it is, the more study, detail and kinds of explanation an adept needs.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the introduction to the series (tape 001), which reads no line: it presents the book and says why the classes begin at chapter 10, so it is placed under the chapter's opening.

blocks.text: Kabbala and *Chassidus* are about G-dliness, the deepest study there is, needing the most. You cannot "just go to a cave someplace and meditate on G-dliness and expect to become an adept": the human mind cannot know it or reach it by its own effort. The only way is the Kabbala G-d gave Moses on Sinai with the written and oral Torah.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the introduction to the series (tape 001), which reads no line: it presents the book and says why the classes begin at chapter 10, so it is placed under the chapter's opening.

blocks.text: *Hisbonenus* needs concentration, during the study, or it brings no benefit, and after it. One learns the *seder hishtalshelus* (the chaining down of the worlds) in all its details: how the four universes, emanation, creation, formation and action, come down from the infinite light, something from nothing, to our physical universe. Then one contemplates it.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the introduction to the series (tape 001), which reads no line: it presents the book and says why the classes begin at chapter 10, so it is placed under the chapter's opening.

blocks.text: In sum, part one: *hisbonenus* is not focusing the mind on one thing but deep analytical study of all the details of the chain of worlds. So the course begins at chapter 10, which starts on what to contemplate.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the introduction to the series (tape 001), which reads no line: it presents the book and says why the classes begin at chapter 10, so it is placed under the chapter's opening.

blocks.text: Before the worlds, their whole space was full of the infinite light of G-dliness. To make room for a world, G-d, so to speak, removed the light from a sphere, emanated into it a very thin line of light, finite compared with the infinite, and through more and more *tzimtzumim* (lessenings of the light) brought it down to our very finite world.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the introduction to the series (tape 001), which reads no line: it presents the book and says why the classes begin at chapter 10, so it is placed under the chapter's opening.

blocks.text: The removal is the first *tzimtzum*. What was left, the *reshimu* (impression), gave the thin line that created the worlds, each with less light, from emanation through creation, formation and action. At the end of action is the world of the *kelipos*, the shells or externalities, sometimes called evil influences, where we are: here evil is possible, and it can seem there is no G-d.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the introduction to the series (tape 001), which reads no line: it presents the book and says why the classes begin at chapter 10, so it is placed under the chapter's opening.

blocks.text: Chapter 10. *Hisbonenus* has to be *derech prat* (in detail), so now he explains all the particulars of the ten *sefiros* of the four worlds.
Every *sefira* divides into particulars of particulars, like *chesed* of *Malchus* of *chachma* of *Malchus* of *chesed*: any five levels, and *v'chahai gavna* ("and the like") means even six.

phrases.he: וענין יחודם והתכללותם בבחינת הכתר שבכל עולם,
phrases.en: How everything is included in the *Keser* of each world,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת הממוצע בין עולם העליון לתחתון הימנו
כידוע הכלל דרך קיצור
שמבחינת מלכות שבעליון נעשה כתר לתחתון, עד רום המעלות.

blocks.text: How all is included in the *Keser* of each world, the link to the one below, since the upper's *Malchus* becomes the lower's *Keser*: chapter 10 to the end of the book explains this.

sections.title: First the Source of everything: the Essence before the tzimtzum, in three levels
sections.summary: Before the worlds, one has to contemplate *Mekora d'Kula*, the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, and that too in particulars. In general it divides into three levels, *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*, each of ten *sefiros*, all still inside the *Atzmus*.

phrases.he: אך הנה מתחלה
phrases.en: However, now that we're getting started, first of all

phrases.he: יש לכל מתבונן להתבונן במקור הראשון
הנקרא מקורא דקולא
phrases.en: the source of everything,

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת עצמות אור אין סוף
שלפני הצמצום הנקרא מקום פנוי הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: before the *tzimtzum*, which is called the *makom panui*.

blocks.text: First the contemplator starts with *Mekora d'Kula*, the source of everything: the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light) before the *tzimtzum* called the *makom panui* (the empty space).

phrases.he: גם שם דרך פרט דוקא
phrases.en: And over there we're also going to look in a way of a *derech prat*.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא מאריך באחד, באחדות הפשוטה דוקא
phrases.en: This is the inner meaning of *ma'arich b'echad* in *Hashem Elokeinu Hashem Echad*: he looks at length *b'achdus hapeshuta davka*.

blocks.text: There too we look *derech prat*: the inner meaning of *ma'arich b'echad*, drawing out the *Echad* of "*Hashem Elokeinu Hashem Echad*", looking at length into the simple oneness.

phrases.he: ונחלק לג' מדריגות דרך כלל
phrases.en: In general we divide it into three levels.

phrases.he: ובכל א' כלול מי׳ ספירות
phrases.en: Each one of them includes within it ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: והוא יחיד ואחד וקדמון,
phrases.en: These three levels: *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*.

phrases.he: והכל בבחינת עצמות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום הראשון הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: This all is still inside the *Atzmus*.

blocks.text: **In general** three levels, really many more: these are only the *pnimiyus ha'or* (the inner aspect of the light), before its *hispashtus* (spreading forth); not the *Maor* (the source of the light) but the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*. Each includes ten *sefiros*: *Yachid* (singular), *Echad* (one) and *Kadmon* (preceding), all still inside the *Atzmus*.

sections.title: Yachid: no ten sefiros, and yet ten sefiros included
sections.summary: *Yachid* is *mamash* alone, above even a unification, so in the Essence one cannot speak of ten *sefiros*. Yet just as speech shows a will and a brain behind it, the Essence includes ten *sefiros*: wise, but not with a wisdom you could separate out. The *middos* come from Him; they do not describe Him.

phrases.he: בחינת יחיד משמעו לבדו ממש
והוא למעלה מהתאחדות נפרדים
שנקרא אחד כידוע
ולפי זה בבחינת העצמות ממש
לא יתכן לומר עדיין ענין עשר ספירות כלל
וכמו מלכות דאין סוף,
שממילא מובן שקדם לזה בחינת כתר וחכמה כו'

blocks.title: Speech means a will and a brain
blocks.text: So in the Essence one cannot yet speak of ten *sefiros*. Compare *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*: *Malchus* is speech, and "you can't have a speech without a *ratzon* (will) and a brain," so *Keser* and *chachma* preceded it.

phrases.he: ובאמת גם בבחינת העצמות דאור אין סוף
שנקרא לבדו
כלול בעצמו י׳ ספירות
אך שנקרא חכים לא בחכמה ידיעא כידוע,
phrases.en: He is wise, but not with a wisdom that can be separated out so you can know that this is the wisdom.

phrases.he: עד ולאו מכל אלין מדות כלל.
phrases.en: It's not just that *lav b'chachma yedia*; it really is not of these *middos* at all.

blocks.text: Even the Essence, called *Levado*, includes ten *sefiros*. *Emek HaMelech* (a Kabbalistic work) calls the *Maor* and the *Levad* levels of *Yachid*, so this is the most external level of *Yachid*, the most inward of the *Or Ein Sof*.

"Wise, but not with a known wisdom": **He is wise, but not with a wisdom that can be separated out so you can know that this is the wisdom.** More, **it really is not of these *middos* at all**: the *middos* come from Him; they do not describe Him.

sections.title: His light as He is, and yet letters engraved: a Keser and a Malchus in the Essence
sections.summary: The *Or Ein Sof* is simple like the Essence, "He and His Name", the *tehiru ila'a*, a revelation of Him to Himself, where even "unity" does not fit. The names wise and kind are only from what He would be after the *tzimtzum*; and yet the Zohar's *glif glifu* puts a head and an end, a *Keser* and a *Malchus*, inside the Essence: "*Ana Emloch*", which the souls of Israel precede.

phrases.he: והענין הוא
דבאמת כמו שעצמות האין סוף הוא אור פשוט בתכלית הפשיטות,
כך ממש בחינת אורו וזיוו הנקרא אור אין סוף
דהיינו הוא ושמו בלבד כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: That means only Him and His name.

blocks.text: First the *Maor*: the Essence is utterly simple light, and so *mamash* (actually) is His light, the *Or Ein Sof*. **That means only Him and His name**: simply, there is no other level; the *bilvad* (only) is a hint to *Levado*. Him is the *Atzmus Ein Sof*; His Name is the *Or Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא טהירו עילאה
שזהו ענין ובחינת התגלות אור עצמותו כמו שהוא דוקא
phrases.en: That is the revelation of the light of Himself, exactly how He is.

blocks.text: This whole matter of the *tehiru ila'a* is everything before the *tzimtzum*. *Kadmon* too is still *tehiru ila'a*, not only *Yachid*.
**That is the revelation of the light of Himself, exactly how He is**. Elsewhere it is explained that this is a revelation to Himself, not yet going out to others: "It's *mamash* to nobody."

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא יחיד,
phrases.en: This is what is called *Yachid*:

phrases.he: שאין עוד מלבדו
phrases.en: there's no more besides Him,

phrases.he: לומר בו לשון התאחדות או לשון יחוד
phrases.en: that you really cannot even call it a unification or a unity.

phrases.he: וזהו אנת הוא חד ולא בחושבן י' כו'.
phrases.en: You are one and not with a *cheshbon*, not with a mathematics. Which mathematics? Ten: that's ten *sefiros*.

blocks.text: **This is what is called *Yachid***: **there's no more besides Him**. But this is its most external part, its *gilui* (revelation), almost its *hispashtus*. So **you really cannot even call it a unification or a unity**; even *Yachid*, a word of *yichud*, is really wrong.
*Ant hu chad v'lo b'chushban*: You are one, and not with a count. Which count? The commentary says ten: **that's ten *sefiros***.

phrases.he: אך מה שאמרו חכים ולא בחכמה ידיעא כו'
phrases.en: So why do they say He is wise, but not with a known wisdom?

phrases.he: שיש על כל פנים חלוקי מדריגות,
חכים ומבין חסדן ורחמן כו'
הכל לא מצד עצמותו,
phrases.en: This thing that we're calling *chacham* is not really that it actually describes Him.

phrases.he: רק מצד מה ששיער בעצמו בכח
מה שעתיד להיות בפועל אחר הצמצום הראשון הנזכר לעיל

blocks.question: Then why say He is wise, but not with a known wisdom, as if He had levels? If there is no *chachma* there, how is He wise?
blocks.text: **This thing that we're calling *chacham* is not really that it actually describes Him**: He made people with *chachma* and *bina*, so you have to call Him wise. But how, if there is no *chachma*?

Of a person, no *chachma* means stupid; of the *Aibershter* (the One Above) it means **not with a known wisdom**, so far beyond yours that you cannot say *chachma* there. More: *chachma* does not define Him; He defines it, and it gets everything from Him, while a *chacham* is defined by being one.

Another thing: as we learned before, *chachma* also means stupidity. *Taanug* (delight) too is the power to have pleasure or the opposite: the ability to feel pain comes from *pnimiyus haKeser* of *Atik*, like the ability to feel pleasure. So the ability to be stupid also comes from Him, and if He is wise, not with a known wisdom, "you'll have to say also he's stupid," not with a known stupidity: a *shtus d'kedusha* (holy foolishness).

sensitivity.reason: Says that G-d is "stupid, not with a known stupidity"; some readers would take the wording as irreverent, like the film joke after it.
sensitivity.publishable: Another thing: as we learned before, *chachma* also includes its opposite. *Taanug* (delight) too is the power to have pleasure or the opposite: the ability to feel pain comes from *pnimiyus haKeser* of *Atik*, like the ability to feel pleasure. So the ability to lack wisdom also comes from Him, and if He is wise, not with a known wisdom, the opposite of wisdom is in Him too, not as you think it: a *shtus d'kedusha* (holy foolishness).

blocks.text: Nobody can beat the *Aibershter*: "If you're going to play a stupid game, the *Aibershter* would win. You know, like they had a movie, *Dumb and Dumber*. If there was a contest who could be the dumbest of them all, the *Aibershter* would win."

sensitivity.reason: A joke that G-d would win a contest for the dumbest, by way of a film comedy; some readers would take it as irreverent.

blocks.text: That belongs to the matter of place: even stupidity needs a place, "otherwise you couldn't have a stupid person." So He gives the *chachma* existence, in both its lines.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב במקדש מלך בלשון האריז''ל עצמו ומבואר במקום אחר באריכות)
phrases.en: This is explained in the *Mikdash Melech*.

phrases.he: וזהו ענין כללות המאמר הראשון בזוהר,
בריש הורמנא דמלכא גליף גליפו בטהירו עילאה
פירוש בעצמות גלוי אורו הפשוט הנזכר לעיל שנקרא טהירו עילאה,
גליף גליפו שהוא ענין חקיקת אותיות
phrases.en: He engraved letters,

blocks.text: **This is explained in the *Mikdash Melech*** (a commentary on the Zohar), a footnote reference. Then the *Zohar*'s first saying: "He engraved an engraving" of letters. Later: within the *ratzon hapashut* (the simple will) is the *ratzon hamuchlat* (the absolute will), the engraving of letters.

phrases.he: ובריש הורמנא,
שזה כשעלה ברצונו הפשוט,
הוא בחינת כתר,
ובחינת האותיות שחקק
הוא בחינת המלכות דאור אין סוף
ואם כן יש ראש וסוף,
כתר ומלכות, גם בבחינת עצמיות אור אין סוף

blocks.text: The simple will that He wants something is *Keser*; the letters He engraved, *Malchus*: so the Essence has a head and an end. And a *chachma*, to figure out letters: "A dog can have a *ratzon* and he can't write it." And *bina* to divide them; presumably, with *bina*, *middos*.

phrases.he: וביאורו
שעלה במחשבה ורצון הפשוט
phrases.en: When it came up in the *ratzon hapashut*

phrases.he: אנא אמלוך
phrases.en: "I will rule."

phrases.he: והכל בעצמותו עדיין,
phrases.en: This is still inside of Himself.

phrases.he: קודם ענין מה ששיער בעצמו בכח דוקא כל מה שיהיה לו רצון למלוכה בגלוי,
phrases.en: This is still before He actually figured out.

phrases.he: והוא אחר הצמצום הנקרא מקום פנוי כו'
phrases.en: The *shiur* is what will be after the *tzimtzum*.

blocks.question: You told us there is no *Keser* and *Malchus* there; now you say there is?
blocks.text: He has done this several times already: there is and there isn't. The explanation: it arose in the thought and the simple will, "*Ana Emloch*" (I shall rule).

blocks.title: With whom did He consult? The Jews before "I shall rule"
blocks.text: He always adds here: *b'mi nimlach?* With whom did He consult? With the souls of the *tzaddikim*, and "Your people are all *tzaddikim*." *Emloch* (rule) and *nimlach* (consult) are basically one word: through whom did He become king? So a Jew's source is in the *Ana Emloch*, above the *machshava kduma* (the primordial thought), and even above the *Ana Emloch*, to which they gave existence. The Jews go all the way up.

All this is still within His Essence, before He figured it out: the *glif glifu* (He engraved an engraving). It has levels, in *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*, where the *shiur* (estimation) is; usually it is called a *shiur*, but this one is before the *shiur*, in the simple will, in *Yachid*. The actual decision for the Jew is in *Yachid*.

And *Yachid* reveals the *Atzmus* exactly as it is, so this came from the *Atzmus*: "Really it's the *Aibershter* that wants the Jew." Otherwise the Jew could not exist, for He is the place of everything and the light cannot do what He gives no place for. It goes higher still, beyond what the text speaks of.
The *shiur* is what will be after the *tzimtzum*. So what is going on? It is a perfect unity with no parts, and we talk about parts.

sections.title: The kind man: a hiyuli desire for kindness that holds every particular
sections.summary: A kind person's kindness is not made of kindnesses for shoes and sandwiches, yet a kindness that lacks one of them is no kindness at all, and every particular, even pants he never gave, comes out of it. So too the ten *sefiros* are in the Essence: not as parts, and not removable, and in the *nimshal* the actual sandwich comes from there.

phrases.he: והדמיון בזה ידוע
מכחות הנפש בהתגלות מרצון עד המעשה
שישנם כולם בפרט
בהעלם אור עצמות הנפש שנקרא בחינת יחידה

blocks.text: The powers are all there in particular. The *yechida* (the essence of the soul) is a unitary thing, not made of powers, yet the powers are there.

phrases.he: כמו על דרך דוגמא
כאשר האדם הוא חפץ חסד וטוב להטיב בדבר פרט,
שזהו בא מצד שיש בו מדה זאת דחפץ חסד וטוב בבחינת עצמות נפשו, הנקרא יחידה
phrases.en: It means that he is a kind person himself.

phrases.he: על כן בא חפץ חסד זה בגלוי מן העלמו
phrases.en: That's why this *chafetz chesed* comes into revelation from its hiddenness.

blocks.text: **It means that he is a kind person himself.** The self is not made of *middos*, true; but he is not himself plus add-ons. He himself is kind, so kindness is there: not a separate thing, yet a particular.

blocks.title: The schnorrers' recommendation
blocks.text:
So it comes out, as the *schnorrers* (beggars) tell each other: go to him, he's a good guy. Do you know the future? No need: he helped me, and Shloimy, and Chaimy.

Not that he *has* a kindness, or "maybe he got hit on the head and the kindness kind of went away." He is good himself. **That's why this *chafetz chesed* comes into revelation from its hiddenness**.

phrases.he: ומוכרח לומר בוודאי
phrases.en: So you have to say for sure

phrases.he: שחפץ חסד זה בעצמות נפשו הוא בבחינת כח היולי בעצמיות
phrases.en: that the *chafetz chesed* is a *hiyuli*,

phrases.he: לכלול כל מה שעתיד לחפוץ בחסד וטוב
phrases.en: any kind of good thing.

phrases.he: בכל פרטי פרטי הענינים שיבקשו ממנו
phrases.en: It includes all the different particular things that people will ask from him.

blocks.title: Shoes, coats, sandwiches, and pants
blocks.text: Not a kindness like this: one needed shoes and got shoes, Chaimy a coat, Shloimy a sandwich. So he has kindnesses for shoes, coats and sandwiches; but I need pants, and he never gave anyone pants. Still, tell him and he'll give you pants. How do you know? Because **the *chafetz chesed* is a *hiyuli***.
It includes all he will ever want of kindness, **any kind of good thing**, every particular asked of him: ask him for pants, and that too is in the *hiyuli*.
At the start of the next side he sums up: the *hiyuli* desire for kindness **includes all the different particular things that people will ask from him**, shoes, sandwiches, whatever.

And if one particular is missing, it is not *chesed*. The essential *chafetz chesed* is not made of *ratzonos* (wills) for sandwiches, shoes and clothing; it is defined by kindness. Yet take out one *prat* (particular) and it is not *chesed* anymore.

So *Pasach Eliyahu* (in the *Tikkunei Zohar*): whoever separates one of these ten *sefiros* from its fellow, it is as if he separated You. The *Atzmus* is not made of *sefiros*, but take out *chesed* and it is not the *Aibershter*: he is a *kofer* (denier) in all of Him.
For instance, to say "G-d is love," with no *din* (judgement), or, as some people say, unconditional love, takes out the attribute of *din*, and the attribute of *din* says there are conditions.

sensitivity.reason: "G-d is love" and "unconditional love" are slogans associated with Christian preaching; the rejection can be read as aimed at another religion.

blocks.text: Like a man who will do anything but give you shoes: walk barefoot, too bad. That is not kindness. So take out one *sefira* and it is not the *Aibershter*: "as if he separated You."

phrases.he: ואם כן בהכרח
phrases.en: So you have to say

phrases.he: שקודם שעלה ברצונו וחפצו זה שבגלוי,
להטיב חסדו בדבר זה הפרטי,
היה כלול בעצמיות חפץ חסד ההיולי
phrases.en: that the *chesed* for shoes was included in the *chafetz chesed hahiyuli*.

phrases.he: ויצא מן ההיולי להתגלות בדבר פרטי זה
phrases.en: And it came out from the *hiyuli* to be *misgaleh* in this particular kindness.

blocks.text: **So you have to say** that a *chesed* for pants was included: how else could one come out? Yet the essential *chafetz chesed* is not made of *chassadim* (kindnesses) for pants, coats and sandwiches. So from one side you have to say they are there.

In the *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for) you *mamash* have to say it. In the *mashal* the *hiyuli* desire holds a *chesed* for sandwiches, not sandwiches, which only a rich man could keep giving. In the *nimshal* the actual sandwich comes from there.

This is what people fail to understand; they make it more and more abstract. In the *mashal* it is stupid to say even that the *chafetz chesed* holds a *chesed* for sandwiches: it is just a *chesed*. But by the *Aibershter* it is the same thing.

blocks.title: Thanking Him for an idea of a sandwich
blocks.text: So He has no sandwiches up there? Then why *bentsh* for a sandwich He gave me? I'd thank whoever gave me the physical sandwich, not an idea of one. Yet we bless before and after: it came from there, so He has sandwiches. "In a way it's a stupid thing to say, but in a way it's a stupid thing to say the opposite also": otherwise where do they come from?

So the *chafetz chesed* is a *hiyuli* power holding all the particulars asked of it. Reading the line again: the *chesed* for sandwiches is in it, so that without it there is no *chafetz chesed* at all. What does that mean?

blocks.title: The foundation that only gives shoes
blocks.text: There are foundations whose charter is to give shoes. A man can "drop dead on the floor from starvation" there, and they will not give him a sandwich: their charter is shoes. It might have started from a kind man who would have given a sandwich too; now it is a foundation, and it gives shoes. Is this a *chesed*? No, it is not a *chesed* anymore.

sensitivity.reason: Charitable foundations are pictured as letting a man starve on their floor because of their charter.
sensitivity.publishable: Picture a foundation whose charter is to give shoes. A starving man asks for a sandwich, and they will not give him one: their charter is shoes. It might have started from a kind man who would have given a sandwich too; now it is a foundation, and it gives shoes. Is this a *chesed*? No, it is not a *chesed* anymore.

blocks.text: A kindness that has become bound by a charter still takes care of shoes, but it does not give because of goodness any more, even though it originated with goodness: "now it is just bureaucracy."
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 003 opens by finishing the foundation example of tape 002 on these lines, before it reads line lwzq6db4 again at 4:43.

sensitivity.reason: Calls charitable foundations a bureaucracy that no longer acts from goodness.
sensitivity.publishable: A kindness that has become bound by a charter still takes care of shoes, but it does not give because of goodness any more, even though it originated with goodness.

blocks.title: Communism, a kindness of Tohu
blocks.text: "Some of the worst, terriblest things in the world came out of goodness," like communism. One might say Marx and Engels were slightly misguided, but their original idea was that everybody's needs should be met; then it got separated from the *Atzmus*. That is *olam haTohu*: no longer a *chesed*, but a *chesed* of *Tohu*. It will give shoes to somebody, and somebody else can *mamash* starve to death and it will not help him.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 003 opens by finishing the foundation example of tape 002 on these lines.

sensitivity.reason: Names communism, and Marx and Engels, among the worst things in the world.

blocks.text: A real *chesed* is not the foundation, of which you cannot say, they are kind, go to them: you need a coat, and they say sorry, we don't give coats. "It's not a *chesed* anymore, it's just a bureaucracy." Without the particular the whole *chesed* is gone: give everything but a sandwich, and you are not kind. So this particular was in the essential *hiyuli* desire, and came out of it.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 003 opens by finishing the foundation example of tape 002 on these lines.

blocks.text: So too by the *Aibershter*. From one side He is above anything; from the other, you have to say that the *Aibershter* has sandwiches. "If he's missing one sandwich, he's not the *Aibershter*."
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 003 opens by finishing the foundation example of tape 002 on these lines.

blocks.text: "And not only kosher sandwiches. He's got *treif* (non-kosher) sandwiches."
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 003 opens by finishing the foundation example of tape 002 on these lines.

sensitivity.reason: Says G-d "has treif sandwiches"; a joke of the same kind as the Dumb and Dumber one, which some readers would take as irreverent.

blocks.title: "He ain't got no money"
blocks.text: "Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold" is read as *chesed* and *gevura*, but really it is literal. In *Shemoneh Esrei* (the eighteen blessings) we ask Him for money: why, if He ain't got no money? What He's got is way past money, and He can give you *mamash* money.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 003 opens by finishing the foundation example of tape 002 on these lines.

phrases.he: ואנו רואים שיש בחפץ חסד זה שכל וחכמה ומדות ומחשבה ודבור ומעשה
phrases.en: We see that when the *chafetz chesed* of the *atzmiyus* comes into actuality, we see that there's a *sechel*.

phrases.he: אם כן ודאי במקור חפץ חסד זה בהעלמו,
כשהיה כלול בעצמיות החפץ חסד ההיולי,
גם כן מהתחלקות שכל ומדות ומחשבה דבור ומעשה שבו
phrases.en: There also had to be a division of these things.

blocks.title: The drunk who says his family is starving
blocks.text: When the essential *chafetz chesed* comes into actuality there is a *sechel* (intellect) in it: you have to figure out exactly how to do the *chesed*. A man tells you his family is starving, but you know he is a drunk: give him money and he will spend it on liquor, come home and beat up his family, and you will have made it worse for them. So you send a bunch of food over to his wife, not to him. That shows there has to be a *sechel*.

sensitivity.reason: The example is a drunk who beats his family.

blocks.text: Doing it takes *middos*, *chesed* and pity felt in the heart; then *machshava* (thought), deciding; *dibur* (speech), telling him; and *maaseh* (action). So ten *sefiros*: *sechel* is *chachma*, then the *middos*, and thought, speech and action are *Malchus*.
**There also had to be a division of these things** in the hidden source, or how could it come out so? The revealed *chesed* has ten *sefiros*, so the hidden one did too.

phrases.he: אבל בבחינת עצמיות חפץ חסד ההיולי,
כמו שהוא קודם שבא עדיין בדבר פרטי,
הגם שבודאי גם שם יש התחלקות שכל ומדות כו',
מכל מקום כלולים ומתאחדים בתכלית

blocks.text: As with the shoes and the sandwiches: not two *chassadim* joined into a bigger one, but really one thing. So too the ten *sefiros* of the essential *chafetz chesed*.

Later he says the same of the *chafetz chesed* in the *Atzmus Ein Sof*: the kindness in a person's *yechida* is no more separate than shoes from sandwiches, or than its ten *sefiros*, nor is it separate from the other *sefiros*, or really from the *Atzmus*.

sections.title: Every attribute alike, down to kingship: "I shall rule"
sections.summary: *Chesed* is only the example; every attribute, *netzach* with its strategy and its pep talk, down to *Malchus*, is made of ten, all one before it comes to a particular. He picked *chesed* and *Malchus* because the world comes from the desire for kindness and from "*Ana Emloch*": there is no king without a people.

phrases.he: וכמו כן במדה פרטית אחרת שבעצמיות,
כמו מדת הגבורה והתפארת והנצח וכהאי גוונא
עד בחינת המלכות
phrases.en: all the way to *Malchus*,

phrases.he: שהוא מדת ההתנשאות
שכלול בודאי מי',
phrases.en: Certainly, same like all the other *sefiros*, it's made up from ten *sefiros*,

phrases.he: רצון וחפץ למלוכה וחכמה ומדות ומחשבה כו'.

blocks.text: *Chafetz chesed* is just the example; every attribute in the essence is so, *gevura*, *tiferes*, *netzach*. A guy who likes to win has *netzach* (victory) in his soul.

blocks.title: The football game
blocks.text: He likes to win all kinds of things, and to win he needs a *sechel* and *middos*: even a football game, stupid as it is, has a strategy.

blocks.title: It's all strategy
blocks.text: Everybody here is into football. He has no idea what they are talking about; when they look to him for a comment, he says, "Yeah, you know, it's all strategy," and they agree.
Strategy means *netzach* needs a *sechel*. Then *middos*: the pep talk before the game builds them up. And *netzach* has thought, speech and action.

Any attribute would do; Rabbi Markel thinks he chose *chesed* because the world comes from *chafetz chesed*. Then down to *Malchus*, the attribute of *hisnasus* the world came from, also made of ten: the will to rule (*Keser*), *chachma*, *middos*, and thought, speech and action, *Malchus* of *Malchus*.

phrases.he: אך קודם שבא לבחינת התגלות בדבר פרט,
phrases.en: But before it became *hisgalus* for a particular thing,

phrases.he: כמו למלוך על מדינה זו וכהאי גוונא,
כלולים ומתאחדים בתכלית
בבחינת מדת המלוכה ההיולית העצמית
כמו בעצמות חפץ חסד ההיולי הנ"ל

blocks.text: Now back to *Ana Emloch*, the *glif glifu*: hence *davka* *Malchus*. *Chafetz chesed* was the arousal from above that brought about a world at all, but the world itself is *Ana Emloch*, *Malchus*, the *glif glifu*, letters: *hisnasus* over another, which brings another into existence. "There is no king without a people."
Before it is revealed in a particular, like ruling this country, there was the original attribute of kingship, its *hiyuli*, before it happened; the particulars are wholly included in it.

sections.title: Not even "unified": the powers within the soul's essence, and where the particulars come from
sections.summary: Tape 004 picks up in mid-discussion (lines 48 to 64 are not recorded): the eye has the power to see every shape, even a sofa some guy in China has, and the will for *chesed* holds a will for every particular, or where would they come from? In the *nimshal* not only the power comes from there: the actual sofa, the actual car, the physical world itself.

phrases.he: מזה מוכרח לומר
שיש כל פרטים הללו בהתפשטות הכלולה בעצם לגמרי,
שאם לא כן מאין נמצאו פרטים הללו בגלוי ההתפשטות
phrases.en: Where did it come from?

blocks.question: The eye has a *hiyuli* for round and square shapes. What about a sofa some guy in China has, which you never saw and never will?
blocks.text: The eye has the power to see that too: the power to see that particular shape already exists in the eye, not only once it is exposed to it, and so in the soul. All the shapes exist in the soul, though as the power to see them, not the actual sofa.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 004 opens in the middle of a discussion, before it reads line 5jn5xeq5; the reading of the lines before it is not recorded, and the discussion leads straight into this line.

blocks.text: So in the *mashal*, a will to give a shoe is not the shoe; in the *nimshal* the actual shoe comes from it, and the actual sofa, and a person's emotions, all of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* down to the final physicality. "Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold": not just the ability to earn money, but the thing itself.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 004 opens in the middle of a discussion, before it reads line 5jn5xeq5; it leads into this line.

blocks.title: Where did my car come from?
blocks.text: Otherwise, where did my car come from? A car in the *Aibershter*, or in the *chesed* a *chesed* to fix someone's car, cannot be said; yet without it the whole *chesed* breaks. To say my car was in the *Aibershter* sounds silly: He is not made of cars. To say it was not means He is not the *Aibershter*: "What, the car came from another *Aibershter*?"
And where did the physical come from? An *Aibershter* with a physical world beside Him is, the *Rambam* says in *Moreh Nevuchim*, the Greek philosophers' mistake. It too had to be there.

How, if there is nothing but Him? As the particulars were in the essential *chesed*: in the *mashal* a *chesed* for a sandwich; in the *nimshal* the sandwich itself, not separate from Him. Otherwise where would the revealed particulars come from?

phrases.he: כמו האור וזיו שכלול בעצם השמש, שיש בו בהעלם כל פרטי אופני זיו המתפשט
phrases.en: When the light was inside the sun, it already had all the particular things.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא ודי למבין.

blocks.text: **When the light was inside the sun, it already had all the particular things**: the green, blue and yellow of sunlight were already in the sun. That ends the general explanation; now, its three levels.

sections.title: Three levels drawn from the yechida: Yachid, Echad, Kadmon
sections.summary: *Yachid*: powers so wholly within the *yechida* that they *mamash* do not exist. *Echad*: powers ready to come out, like Avraham sitting at his tent with nobody yet come; here they are a unity of many abilities. *Kadmon*: the exact estimate of one act, complete even when something stops it, like the hand already set for the bottle that someone else grabs.

phrases.he: ונמצא ג' מדריגות זה אחר זה נמשך מעצמיות הנפש ממש,
הנקרא בחינת יחידה
הא' י' כחות עצמיים והיוליים,
כמו חפץ חסד העצמי והיולי וכהאי גוונא
כלולים בה בתכלית,
כהתכללות כח התנועה בעצם החי
וכהתכללות התפשטות החיות בעצם כנזכר לעיל
ולא יתכן בהם לומר לשון התאחדות מדברים נבדלים יחד
phrases.en: You can't even say it's a unification.

phrases.he: אחר שכלולים לגמרי בעצם,
והיה כלא היה במציאות כלל וכלל כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: It's like they *mamash* don't exist, totally; like we explained before.

blocks.text: This is *Yachid*: wholly included, they *mamash* do not exist. Like the power of movement in the living being, the *yechida* is not in their bounds or their category: **You can't even say it's a unification.** **It's like they *mamash* don't exist, totally**.

phrases.he: והב' בחינת התפשטות י' כחות שמוכנים לבא בבחינת גלוי
phrases.en: It's a thing of *hispashtus*, that it's *muchan* to come out in various ways, like *chesed* or whatever of the ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: כמו חפץ חסד העצמי ההיולי שבא לדבר חסד בדרך פרט
גם קודם שנמשך בפועל ממש, רק כשעתיד ומוכן לצאת לדבר פרט
phrases.en: There's a point where it's *muchan* to come out to a *prat*, but you don't have a *prat* yet.

blocks.text: The second is *Echad*. It is already a thing of *hispashtus* (spreading forth): it is ready to come out in various ways, like *chesed*, or whichever of the ten *sefiros*.

blocks.title: Avraham sitting by the tent
blocks.text: Like *Avraham Avinu* sitting by the tent, ready for a *chesed*, but nobody has come yet. Ready to come out to a particular, with no particular yet: that is *Echad*.

phrases.he: שם יתכן ענין האחדות מכמה פרטים שבו
phrases.en: There you can say that it's made of various things,

phrases.he: כמו שכל ומדות שבחפץ חסד זה
הנמשך מהעלמות ההיולי הכללי כו'.

blocks.text: **There you can say that it's made of various things**, intellect and *middos* in the desire for kindness, though not *mamash* a unification. Powers that did not exist at all in the essence reach a point of ability to exist, not yet existence: that is *Echad*, an ability made of many, unified as the soul's general *hispashtus*.

phrases.he: והג' כשנמשך ובא לאותו דבר פרט,
רק שעדיין לא בא מצד העדר ומניעה

blocks.text: Not only when it does not come: when nothing hinders and you act, this third level joins the act. But it is *davka* when absence and hindrance stop it that you can see it.

blocks.title: The bottle on the farbrengen table
blocks.text:
At a *farbrengen* (a Chassidic gathering) your glass is empty and you reach for the bottle of vodka on the table. The whole movement is in the power of movement before you make it, so you don't grope; you know where your hand will go. Just then somebody else grabs the bottle.

It stayed a *hiyuli*, yet it was completely prepared; had he grabbed it, the same preparation would join the grabbing. So the absence is not necessarily an absence: that is only how you see it, from the absence and the hindrance.

phrases.he: אבל ההכנה בעצמה כבר בשלימותה,
phrases.en: but the preparation is all complete,

phrases.he: ולא חסר רק לבא בהתגלות בפועל ממש
דהיינו שכבר שיער היטב בעצמו בדרך פרט
לאותו דבר שבא לפועל ממש
והיינו שיער בעצמו בכח מה שצריך להביא בפועל

blocks.text: The preparation itself is already complete, lacking only revelation in actual deed: he has already estimated in himself, in particular, what comes into actual deed, here to grab the bottle.

sections.title: The examples, and the contraction that brings the spiritual into the physical
sections.summary: The power of movement, the spirit of life and the power of growth each have the three levels, and all three are joined even to the deed: one grabs the bottle with the *yechida* itself. Yet the deed is physical, a different thing, and getting there needs a *tzimtzum*; without it a man freezes, or cannot get a word out.

phrases.he: כמו על דרך דוגמא הנזכר לעיל בכח התנועה
כשעתידה לצאת בגלוי בדבר פרט

blocks.text: The power of movement as it is about to come out, to grab a bottle, for instance. So even if he did make the movement, it is connected to this third level.

blocks.title: "When you're finished, pass the bottle over"
blocks.text: The other guy grabbed it, so he says, "When you're finished, pass the bottle over." The power of movement, in the soul's essence just a desire for a drink of vodka, turned into the power of speech, *mamash* the same thing: in *Kadmon* *mamash* one, yet powers unified as one. Ready to grab the bottle became asking for it.
So when it does not happen, you see it was all prepared, yet need not happen; when it does, the *hiyuli* stays a *hiyuli*. And one power can turn into another.

phrases.he: וכן מה ששיער התגלות התפשטות רוח החיים,
phrases.en: when he is *meshaer* how much revelation of the *ruach hachayim* is going to be,

phrases.he: והוכן בו מה שעתיד להחיות בפועל ממש
phrases.en: and it's already included what he is *asid lehachayos* in *poel mamash*

blocks.title: "Liven up, we got a big job ahead of us"
blocks.text: What he will enliven in actual deed is already included when he estimates how much of the spirit of life to reveal: psyching himself up to run, he needs an extra influx of life, "like they tell the soldiers, liven up, we got a big job ahead of us."

phrases.he: וכמו כן דמיון כח הצומח כשמוכן להצמיח בפועל ממש,
phrases.en: The same thing, like the *koach hatzomeach* in the ground, when it's *mamash* already connected to a tree and it's ready to actually give this tree the power to grow:

phrases.he: שיש בזה גם כן ענין ג' מדריגות הללו
phrases.en: each one of these *kochos* has these three *madreigos*.

blocks.text: So too the power of growth in the ground, ready to make a tree grow: each power has these three levels, all connected to the deed: the deed to *Kadmon*, *Kadmon* to *Echad*, *Echad* to *Yachid*.

Grabbing for the bottle, "really he's grabbing it with *Yachid*," the essence of the *yechida*, through two conduits: *Echad*, where the powers come out in particular, and *Kadmon*, where they come out for this action, where it is estimated.

phrases.he: והכל הוא טרם שבא הדבר עדיין בפועל ממש
כמו התנועה קודם שבאה בגשם הנפעל
או החיות הרוחני קודם שבא בגשם הגוף
ששם משתנה ממהות רוחנית למהות גשם,
phrases.en: Where it actually comes into an actual *tnua*, a *tnua* is not anymore the thing of the soul; it's a physical movement.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת תנועה גשמיות
phrases.en: That's a physical *tnua*.

phrases.he: והחיות גשמיות
וכהאי גוונא בגשם הצמיחה כו'
phrases.en: the actual plant.

blocks.text: This is not the coming out into actual deed; even when it comes out into the deed, this is the inner power, which does not come into the deed.
In an actual movement, the movement and its life are physical, no longer the soul's. So **the actual plant** is not the power of growth but another thing, a plant, like a piece of wood.

phrases.he: שצריך לזה בחינת צמצום וכיווץ בגלוי זה הרוחני בתחלה, כדי שיבוא מכלל רוחניות לגשמיות
phrases.en: In order to come from the spiritual to the physical, you have to make a *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: (כמו שיתבאר באות הי''ב):
phrases.en: This will be explained, *b'ezras Hashem*, in chapter 12.

blocks.title: Costello and the Wolf Man
blocks.text: To come into physicality, the spiritual must first be contracted. Abbott and Costello and the Wolf Man (Abbott is the tall straight man): with the Wolf Man behind Abbott, Costello sputters (he acts it out). So panicked, he cannot *metzamtzem* (contract) his speech into particular letters; he wants it all out at one shot. Without a *tzimtzum*, there is no particular thing.

blocks.title: Frozen before a Tyrannosaurus Rex
blocks.text: So with a Tyrannosaurus Rex looming over you on the street: people freeze when they should run. The shock brings out the whole power of movement at one shot, with no *tzimtzum* into one movement, which way to go; trying to run every way at once, he runs none.

So in many things. Without the *tzimtzum*, the spiritual power is infinite, not for a particular movement, and speech is not for a particular thing; the *tzimtzum* must go all the way down to the letters.
That is also why people stutter: they are trying to put the whole thought into speech at one shot, without the *tzimtzum*, and you have to teach them to slow down and make a *tzimtzum*.

sensitivity.reason: Gives a cause of stuttering and a way to treat it ("teach them how to slow down"), which a reader might act on.

blocks.text: So to come from the spiritual to the physical you have to make a *tzimtzum*, as will be explained with G-d's help in chapter 12.

Summing up: some places say nothing is in the *Or Ein Sof*, no count of ten *sefiros*, no attribute at all. Others say He engraved an engraving in the *tehiru ila'a* (letters), the simple will, the head of the King's authority, wise but not with a known wisdom (so, a *chachma*). Which is it?

No *sefiros* means not lacking them but totally higher: no more an actual *chachma* there than a will for shoes in a *chesed*. Yet you cannot take them out: to say there is no *chachma* at all calls the *Aibershter* stupid, and separating one *sefira* makes you a *kofer b'ikar* (one who denies the essence), *mamash kofer* in the *Aibershter*.

blocks.title: "I don't do shoes"
blocks.text: Like the *chesed* we spoke of: he has a fund for coats and one for feeding people, but "I don't do shoes." A poor man stands before you with bleeding feet and you won't do shoes: you *mamash* don't have *chesed*, you are not an *ish chesed* (a man of kindness), whatever else you do. A *chesed* is not made of a *chesed* for shoes, but take out this piece and you took out the whole thing.

So though there are no ten *sefiros* up there, believe all is there except *netzach* of *tiferes*, one *sefira* of a *sefira*, and you are totally *kofer* in the *ikar*. The basic point is the line's question: otherwise, where would these particulars come from?

reviewQuestions.question: Why does the introduction insist that *hisbonenus* is *iyun* and not meditation, and why must it be done in particulars?
Why is even the name *Yachid* not quite right for the first level?
What does "wise, but not with a known wisdom" mean, and why may one not simply say there is no *chachma* there?
How do the *schnorrers* know a man will help them, and how do they know he will give pants he never gave anyone?
Why is a foundation that gives only shoes no longer a *chesed*, and what does that teach about taking one *sefira* out of the Essence?
What does the bottle of vodka at a *farbrengen* show about *Kadmon*, and what happens when someone else grabs it first?

notes.text: Class 001 (the series introduction) reads no line; its blocks are placed under the first passage with outOfPlace. Its times are Sofer's, not re-timed.
"Over there if you look in the Emek HaMelech he says in Yachid he calls the Maor and the Levad levels of Yachid": compressed in the transcript; reported as far as it is clear.
"that's what elu parshiyos told us" (002, 6:29) is unclear; left out of the block.

"like what we learned before of the beis kavvan v'shkulin, chachma means also stupidity" looks misheard; the block keeps only that chachma also includes its opposite, "both lines". Likewise "the place" ("one of the things that we're talking about the place") probably refers to an earlier class.

The end of tape 002 (from 28:00) is aligned to line ohjliorz at low confidence (0.38). It is a second reading of line uzqwele2 and the foundation example, so it is placed under uzqwele2-6dpx7uzu, with the opening of tape 003 that finishes it.
Tape 003 rereads lines lwzq6db4-6dpx7uzu (from 4:43, "I'm going to start from the third line here"); its comments are placed under those passages.

Line 47: he reads "b'koach b'atzmo koach hasirtuta hahiyuli" (likely misheard) and says only "the same thing, like we said before". In line 46, "which really existed even before the kli peula" is unclear and left out.

No recording covers lines qujawkgb-kcyvcac3: tape 003 ends after line ctm4eaq3 and tape 004 opens mid-discussion (the eye's power to see a sofa in China), just before line 5jn5xeq5. Those passages have no phrases.
Lines bn74tlmj-uwqzjjvc are not read: after line oty7ghqk tape 004 goes straight to line cm6dr6ig (12:42). That passage has no phrases.
In the Costello example the transcript drops the sound he makes; the block says he acts it out.
After line wtihx72y the tape runs on (18:49): a summary of chapter 10, cited as recap blocks under the last passage, then a fresh start on line qxeqdrfr before he realises the chapter is finished.

A phrase has English only where he translates it in class, anchored to where he says it; a phrase he only reads keeps its Hebrew alone. Where he gives his English in a later telling (tape 003's reread of lines 37-40, the end-of-chapter recap on tape 004), the anchor points there. He reads some lines with small differences from the printed text (e.g. line 4 "amuda d'bein" for "hamemutza bein", line 88 "b'gashem hanefesh" for "b'gashem hanif'al"); the phrases follow the printed text.
"Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold" (Haggai 2:8) is cited by him without source; "it's translated to mean chesed and gevura" as he gave it.

terms holds the untabled terms first (Levado, bilvad, chacham, metzamtzem, nimlach, bentsh, treif, ish chesed) with Yachid, Echad, Kadmon and hiyuli, which translit.json has but which are the chapter's key terms. Untabled terms left out for the 12-entry cap, each glossed at its first use in the prose: ratzonos (wills), v'chahai gavna (and the like), Ant hu chad v'lo b'chushban, Levad, shtus d'kedusha.

Sensitivity rule for irreverent wording about G-d: a joke or a phrasing that makes Him sound stupid or unkosher is flagged (the Dumb and Dumber aside, the treif-sandwich line, and "He is stupid, not with a known stupidity"). "So the Aibershter is stupid?" in the end-of-chapter recap is not flagged: there he calls that conclusion an insult.
The summary of the section on lines 48-69 is written from tape 004 only; the section title ("Not even 'unified'") follows the unrecorded text of lines 48-64.
